newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS-E.Europe bourses lose steam in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-E.Europe bourses lose steam in profit-taking.

text.p: East and Central European bourses were in a bearish mood at the end of the week as a round of profit-taking hit the markets following steep gains since the beginning of the year.

Some analysts said comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on a possibility of higher U.S. interest rates might also have tempered international players' appetite for emerging market stocks.
Warsaw, Prague and Budapest closed lower, Croatian shares stabilised and Bratislava, Romanian and Slovenian shares were the only ones to buck the trend.
PRAGUE
Blue chip gains pushed the Prague bourse to a two-year high by Tuesday, but it promptly retreated as a round of profit taking gathered momentum by the close of Friday's session.
The PX50 index, which had shot up over 16 percent this year, ended the week 2.61 percent lower at 609.2.
Leading the bourse lower were its three biggest issues -- SPT Telecom a.s., power utility CEZ a.s. and Komercni Banka a.s. -- each of which fell as investors took profits.

"It's a very thin market and when you see a little profit-taking as we are, the market kind of collapses," said Jan Sykora of brokers Wood and Company. "I am afraid that the trend will probably continue."
WARSAW

The Warsaw bourse fell 3.3 percent this week but revived post-fixing buying on Friday signalled at least a brief rebound. Analysts were split however on whether the market would see more profit-taking after the bourse's 30 percent rise since the beginning of the year or a flat trend would emerge.
Some analysts said Greenspan's comments might have helped spark the long-expected correction. BUDAPEST
Hungarian shares closed lower as slight gains in light trade in the first half of the week were swept away on Friday as the market nervously reacted to panic withdrawals by Postabank customers.
Some traders blamed the market's bearish mood on Greenspan's remarks.

Traders said many buyers sat on their hands, fearing a rise in U.S. rates, which would cool international markets and spill over onto the Budapest bourse, which is dominated by foreign players. BRATISLAVA
Major Slovak shares extended last week's gains as they crawled to new year highs on Monday and Wednesday in thin volumes retreated on Thursday to close again higher on Friday.
Brokers said continued demand for the most heavily- weighted issues, such as oil refiner Slovnaft or steel maker VSZ, helped the bourse continue its rise.
Some dealers, however, said the bourse had risen for too long and was now vulnerable to profit-taking. ZAGREB
Croatian stocks closed the week mixed in slow trade and market participants foresaw lower prices would dominate the following week.
Traders said latest unrest in the neighbouring Bosnia helped weaken the demand.
Blue chips, drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka ordinary shares fell 4.3 and 6.3 percent respectively throughout the week.
BUCHAREST

Heavy trading in Bucharest first-tier stocks Oltchim chemical plant and fertiliser maker Azomures kept session turnover at above two billion lei and pushed two market indices to all-time highs on Thursday.
Most other share prices drifted higher due to low supply.
LJUBLJANA

Slovenian shares bounced higher on Friday as the market welcomed the approval of a new government and on hopes that the end to the political impasse may encourage foreign investors to return. The new government was voted in late on Thursday. CLOSE WEEK'S CHANGE 97 HIGH 97 LOW
